t: This is The Wolseley, a restaurant at 160 Piccadilly, right next to The Ritz. The Grade II* listed building was put up in 1921 by Wolseley Motors as their offices, with a car showroom on the ground floor. Its architect was William Curtis Green, who also designed the Dorchester Hotel and New Scotland Yard, and who received the Royal Gold Medal in 1942. From 1927 to 1999 the ground floor was a Barclays bank. After a brief spell as a Chinese restaurant, Chris Corbin and Jeremy King reopened it as the Wolseley in 2003.
